utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the fourth from the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender this record into evidence as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The Prosecution renews the objection, given that the Prosecution was not given time to read the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this -- it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May the witness please be given the next document. Can we please have the next --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D149/1; the name is Mrsic Radovan, dated 12 January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, is this a record of the commission whose member you were and which conducted the investigation of this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is a record of the investigation of the Military Investigating Commission of the 4th Corps and I was a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this document signed by members of the commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see signatures of the members of the commission on this record and I recognise my own signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, was this witness questioned in a legal way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall the questioning of this witness. It was a long time ago, but I say that all these individuals were questioned in a legal manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a comment at the end of this record that the person who was questioned here gave this statement of their own free will?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I move to tender this record which the witness has identified as his own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You omitted to ask one question -- was it signed by the person who gave the statement in his presence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard the question. Would you please answer His Honour? Were these records or statements signed in the presence of the person who was questioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After questioning of a witness, all records were signed by the members of the investigating commission, by the record taker and by the questioned person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I raise the same objection for the record, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown the next record and can the number and the name of the person who was questioned be given?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The record of the statement of witness Kuljanin Marko, dated 11 January 1993, Defence Exhibit D150/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I hope you are not going through the 105 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How many statements do you have?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, during my own investigation, I was not able to collect all 105. I think I have about 10, so there are not that many left. Mr. Begtasovic, do you recognise in this record a record of the commission of which you were a member when you were questioning this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise a record of the Military Investigating Commission of the 4th Corps of which I was a member of 11 January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this record signed by the members of the commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The record was signed by the members of the commission, and I recognise my own signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this witness questioned in a legal way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me repeat that all witnesses were questioned in a legal way. I do not recall the questioning of this witness, either, but I say that he was questioned in a legal manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, as His Honour Judge Jan asked a moment ago, was the witness, that is, the suspect -- was the suspect present as you were signing this record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since the witness recognised his own signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Did the suspect sign the statement in his presence -- that is the question. You just put it a different way -- whether he was present while you were signing it -- whether in fact he signed the statement in his presence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you understand the question of His Honour? Did the suspect sign the record in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did understand the question of His Honour and I can say that, as far as the procedure about signing of records, out of all the listed persons, that is, the members of the commission, the record taker and the suspect, as a rule, the suspect was always the first who signed the record -- only after this person would sign it, then members of the commission would sign it themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to specify this: does that mean that all persons who signed these records, did they all sign it in your presence while you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender this record into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me state again and let the record reflect that the Prosecution was not given time to read the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The elementary things are clear -- you can raise your objections as to their validity. Nothing stops you doing that. If you can demonstrate that they have not complied with the Rules, you are entitled to exclude it. They are admissible on the face of it. Everything is regular.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May the witness be shown the next document and if you could please state the usual things.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know whether the multiplication makes any difference at all, other than showing a particular thing happened -- the statements were taken regularly by persons to whom they were read over by who took them. You can carry on and complete the number of statements you wish to tender but I do not think it makes any difference. It normally does not really matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can only ask, since all the statements are marked individually, they could all be given to the witness as a batch. He can review them and he can confirm them or not, and they can then all be admitted into evidence. We do not have any additional ones. Maybe it would be the best thing if the witness just reviewed all of them at one time together and then they could be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are admitting them separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that is sufficient for their admissibility -- they have all been admitted into evidence so far, those which you have tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours, but I did not understand you. Were you asking whether I needed to continue -- I have another five or six of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may, if you consider they are relevant to your case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. May the witness please be shown the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Statement of the interview with Mrkajic Goran dated 14 January 1993, the Defence Exhibit D151/1. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, I have the same question for you. Do you recognise this as a record of the commission of which you were a member? Was this record signed, do you recognise your signature? Is the person who was interviewed -- did the person who was interviewed sign it in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise the record of the Military Investigating Commission of the 4th Corps of 14 January 1993. On the record I recognise my own signature. It is fourth, but under number 5. I also see the signature of the interviewed person on the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender this record into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, may the witness be shown the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Record of interview with Kuljanin Radovan, made on 14 January 1993, Defence Exhibit D152/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, please review this record and I have the same set of questions for you. Is this a record of the commission of which you were a member? Did you interview this person? Was this record signed? Do you recognise your own signature? Did the person who was interviewed sign it in your presence? Was it a legal procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a record of the commission of which I was a member and I recognise my own signature as fourth from the top. I also see the signature of a person who was interviewed and I also assert that this person was also questioned in a legal manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender this record into evidence. Is it admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I have the next record shown to the witness please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The record of the interview with Kuljanin Jovo made on 18 January 1993, Defence Exhibit D153/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, please, can you answer the questions which are the same questions asked before. Was this a record of your commission? Did you sign it? Was this individual questioned in a legal manner? Did he sign the record in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a record of the Military Investigating Commission of the 4th Corps of which I was a member and, as I can see it, it was made on 18 January 1993. I recognise my own signature as fourth from the top. I see that the person who was interviewed did sign it and I assert that this person was questioned in a legal way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender it into evidence, please as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, shall I continue with a few records that I have left, or have you reached the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us complete this process. We will adjourn after this process.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please would you show the witness the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Record of interview with Kuljanin Dragan made on 18 January 1993, the Defence Exhibit D154/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, could you please answer -- is this a record made by your commission? Has it been signed? Was it produced through a legal procedure, and did this person sign it in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a record of a Military Investigating Commission of the 4th Corps of which I was a member of 18 January 1993. I recognise my own signature fourth from the top and I see that the questioned person did sign it and I assert that the person was questioned in a legal manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender it into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The next record, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Record of interview with Kuljanin Danilo made on 14 January 1993, the Defence Exhibit D155/1. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, is this a record of the commission of which you were a member? Was this record signed? Did you sign it? Did the interviewed person sign it in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a record of the Military Investigating Commission of 14 January 1993. I signed this record, fourth from the top. I see that the interviewed person did sign this record and I assert that this person was questioned in a legal way and that following the questioning he signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can it please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, it is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please can you show the witness the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The record of the interview with Gligorevic Bosko made on 13 January 1993, the Defence Exhibit D156/1. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, would you look at the record? Can you tell me, is this a record of the commission of which you were a member? Was the record signed? Do you recognise your own signature? Did the questioning -- was the questioning conducted in a legal manner and did the questioned person sign the record in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am looking at the record of the Military Investigating Commission compiled on 13 January 1993. I recognise my own signature on it, it is fourth from the top, and I see that the record was also signed by the interviewed person and I assert that the person was questioned in a legal way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender this into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown the next record?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The record of the interview with Bozic Miroslav made on 13 January 1993, Defence Exhibit D157/1. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, can you tell me whether this is a record of the commission of which you were a member? Did you sign this record? Was the record signed by the questioned person in your presence and was the procedure conducted in a regular legal way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a record of the military commission of which I was a member. I recognise my signature as fourth from the top at the end of the statement -- the interviewed person did sign the record and I say that he was questioned in a legal way and that he signed the record after the questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I move to admit it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May the witness please be given the next record.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Record of interview with Stevan Gligorevic made 14 January 1992, Defence Exhibit D158/1. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a record of the commission of which you were a member? Was the person interviewed in a legal way? Did you sign the record? Did the interviewed person sign the record in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a record of the Military Investigating Commission of which I was a member. I recognise my own signature. It is fourth from the top at the end of the statement. The record was also signed by the interviewed person and I assert that the questioning was conducted in a legal way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I move to tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I have the last document shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Record of interview with Kuljanin Jovan, made 11 January 1993, Defence Exhibit D159/1. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begtasovic, can you tell me whether this is a record of the commission of which you were a member, whether the person was interviewed in a legal manner, whether you signed the record, and whether the person signed the record in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a record of the commission of which I was a member. I recognise my own signature. This record also has my signature as fourth from the top -- at the end of the statement I see the interviewed person also signed the record. I assert that this person was also questioned in a legal way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I move to admit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this be an appropriate time to recess?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we will stop here and adjourn until Monday for a continuation. The Trial Chamber will now adjourn. (At 5.40pm the matter adjourned until Monday, 6 April 1998, at 10am)
